data.plain_english: A news story reported that some Hong Kong homeowners are selling their flats for less than they paid, even though there are signs the market is recovering. Hong Kong shares also fell sharply in one day, and borrowing there is still expensive. The council expects Hong Kong property, banks and technology companies to do worse, because high interest rates and weak sentiment weigh on them. In the US, higher interest rates are hurting some industries, but technology has held up, and that is where the council disagrees most. Mainland China and energy views are mostly on the fence, and this is research to help you think, not advice to buy or sell.

risk.method: council view 35% (negative views only), volatility 25% (8-25%), 1-month drawdown 20% (0 to -6%), disagreement 10%, unverified claims 10%; portfolio adds up to 10 points for market concentration
